higher levels of inflammatory factors, sICAM- 1 and sVEGF-2, and lower levels of the anti-inflammatory PEDF are observed in patients with CRVO with SRD.
the vitreous level of sICM-1 and sVegfR-2 was increased, while the vitreous levels of PEDF decreased in patients with CRVO complicated with SRD.
the levels of sICAM1 and sVEGF2 increased, and that of PEDF decreased, in the vitreous humor of patients with CRVO with SRD compared to those with CME.

the relationship between the inflammatory factor in the vitreous and serous retinopathy.
the vitreous inflammatory factors and SRD in CRVO.
the inflammatory factors of the vitreous in the pathogenesis of SRD in CRVO.

the inflammatory factors sICAM- 1 and sVEGF-2 and the anti-inflammatory factor PEDF are associated with the occurrence and severity of SRD in CRVO.
the presence of SRD in patients with CRVO is associated with a more severe form of the disease.
the presence of SRD is a sign of a more severe CRVO, which is characterized by more extensive ischemia, higher levels of inflammatory factors, and lower levels of PEDF.

the vitreous levels of inflammatory factors and anti-inflammatory molecules may be used to predict the occurrence of SRD in CRVO patients.
